## Overview

This week will focus on working with files in the Unix shell.
As we're going to work with (DNA/RNA/protein) sequence files,
we will start with an introduction to the various types of files as well as
the specific files from the example dataset you'll work with throughout the course.

## Learning goals & lectures

##### [**Sequence file types and the example dataset**](./w3a_file-overview.qmd) _(Tuesday)_

- What FASTA, FASTQ, and GFF/GTF files are for and look like
- How quality scores are coded in FASTQ files
- What the experimental design the course's example dataset's study looks like
- Which files are in our example data set

Next, you will learn to use Unix shell commands to:

##### [**Working with files in the Unix shell I: The shell as a file browser**](./w3b_shellfiles.qmd) _(Tuesday)_

- Create, copy, move, rename and delete directories and files

##### [**Working with files in the Unix shell II: Viewing, summarizing and manipulating files**](./w3c_shellfiles.qmd) _(Thursday)_

- View the contents of text files in various ways
- Search within, manipulate, and extract information from text files

## Readings

- @garrigós2025:
 _Two avian Plasmodium species trigger different transcriptional tesponses on their vector Culex pipiens_\
 This is the paper associated with the dataset we will use throughout the course,
 starting this week.
